# The closed torus generated by two commuting tori

Worker 224. This is an internal derivation from published Library results. It is a helper for the
proof of `Langlands.Geometry.Building.SpecialTorusExistenceStatement` (Kaletha–Prasad,
Proposition 9.3.4). There the maximal split torus `S` and the generic fibre `T₁` of a lifted
torus are combined into one closed torus. The module makes no independent literature assertion.

Let `k` be a field, `G` an affine group over `Spec k` and `K` a field extension of `k`.

`exists_closedTorus_of_commute`: let `S` be a commutative group with `iS : S ⟶ G` and `T₁` a
group with `t₁ : T₁ ⟶ G`. Assume the values `x ≫ iS` and `y ≫ t₁` commute for all points `x`, `y`
over every test scheme, and that the base changes `S_K` and `(T₁)_K` are split tori. Then there
are a commutative group `T`, a closed subgroup `iT : T ⟶ G` and homomorphisms `f : S ⟶ T`,
`g : T₁ ⟶ T` with `f ≫ iT = iS` and `g ≫ iT = t₁`, and `T_K` is a split torus.

Proof. Put `E := S × T₁`. Its base change `E_K` is split, because `baseChangeTensorIso`
identifies it with `S_K × (T₁)_K` (`IsSplitTorus.tensor`). So `E` is a torus over `k` in the
Library sense (`IsTorus`: split over some field extension). The commuting values give the
product homomorphism `e := prodHom iS t₁ : E ⟶ G`, `(x, y) ↦ iS(x) · t₁(y)`. Let `T` be its
schematic image `SchematicImage.image e`, with closed inclusion `iT` and projection
`p : E ⟶ T`, `p ≫ iT = e`. `IsTorus.isTorus_schematicImage` shows that `T` is a torus, and hence
commutative (`IsTorus.isCommMonObj`). The maps are `f := prodInl ≫ p` and `g := prodInr ≫ p`,
and `prodInl_prodHom`, `prodInr_prodHom` give the two factorizations. Finally, `K` is flat
over `k`, so the base change of the schematically dominant `p` stays schematically dominant
(`isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant_baseChange`). Then `T_K` is a schematically dominant image of the
split torus `E_K` and is split by `IsSplitTorus.of_schematicallyDominant_hom`.

`card_le_card_of_comp_isClosedSubgroup`: if `g : A ⟶ B` and `i : B ⟶ G` are homomorphisms with
`g ≫ i` a closed subgroup, `A ≅ splitTorus I` and `B ≅ splitTorus J`, then
`Nat.card I ≤ Nat.card J`. The closed immersion `g ≫ i` is a monomorphism, hence so is `g`. The
composite `splitTorus I ≅ A ⟶ B ≅ splitTorus J` is then a monomorphism, and
`splitTorus.card_le_card_of_mono` applies.
